name: Chapter 3: Balance sheet: Liabilities and Equity

questions.text: What is the central economic difference between debt and equity?

options.a: Debt generally creates contractual payment obligations, whereas equity is a residual ownership claim
options.b: Debt and equity necessarily have identical liquidation rights
options.c: Equity always requires fixed periodic interest payments
options.d: Debt gives creditors unlimited residual profits after liquidation

questions.text: According to the course's classification flowchart, a financial instrument requiring the issuer to pay cash is generally what?

options.a: Retained earnings
options.b: An intangible asset
options.c: Other comprehensive income
options.d: A financial liability

questions.text: How are liabilities divided by maturity in the chapter?

options.a: Goodwill and intangible assets
options.b: Cash and cash equivalents
options.c: Operating liabilities and retained earnings only
options.d: Current liabilities and non-current liabilities

questions.text: What is a current maturity of long-term debt?

options.a: All interest scheduled after ten years
options.b: An equity dividend payable at the issuer's discretion
options.c: The portion of long-term principal due within one year
options.d: The original amount of any long-term loan, regardless of due date

questions.text: What is accounts payable?

options.a: The cash paid to repurchase shares
options.b: Amounts due from customers for sales on credit
options.c: Unrealized gains on marketable securities
options.d: Amounts owed to suppliers for purchases made on credit

questions.text: Why is trade credit important to companies with extensive supply chains?

options.a: It ensures suppliers are paid before deliveries
options.b: It prevents the need to manage inventories
options.c: Purchases from suppliers can provide a significant short-term financing source
options.d: It converts all trade creditors into shareholders

questions.text: What does days payable outstanding (DPO) measure?

options.a: Average period the firm takes to pay trade suppliers
options.b: Average days inventory sits in the warehouse
options.c: Average period it takes customers to pay the company
options.d: Time between issuing and redeeming ordinary shares

questions.text: In the lecture's simplified DPO calculation, what is accounts payable turnover?

options.a: Accounts receivable divided by sales
options.b: EBIT divided by gross interest expense
options.c: Cost of goods sold divided by average inventory
options.d: Sales divided by average accounts payable

questions.text: How is DPO obtained from accounts payable turnover?

options.a: 365 multiplied by inventory turnover
options.b: Payable turnover divided by 365
options.c: Sales divided by net income
options.d: 365 divided by payable turnover

questions.text: How does a higher DPO generally affect cash held by the purchasing company in the short run?

options.a: It immediately reduces cash balances
options.b: It forces an identical increase in inventory
options.c: It necessarily increases customer receivables
options.d: It retains cash for longer before paying suppliers

questions.text: What is the potential downside of an extremely high DPO?

options.a: Strained supplier relations and disruption of trade credit
options.b: An automatic decrease in all interest rates
options.c: Automatic improvement in supplier trust
options.d: A guaranteed increase in supplier discounts

questions.text: What is the cash conversion cycle (CCC)?

options.a: DIO - Current ratio
options.b: DSO + DIO - DPO
options.c: DSO + Inventory turnover + Debt ratio
options.d: DPO + ROE - Gross margin

questions.text: Which change shortens the cash conversion cycle, all else equal?

options.a: Higher accounts receivable days
options.b: Lower DPO
options.c: Higher DIO
options.d: Lower DSO

questions.text: How does faster collection from customers affect the cash conversion cycle?

options.a: It leaves the cycle unchanged
options.b: It eliminates trade payables
options.c: It shortens the cycle
options.d: It lengthens the cycle

questions.text: Why may a negative cash conversion cycle be advantageous?

options.a: The firm can receive customer cash before paying suppliers
options.b: The firm must be reporting negative net income
options.c: Inventory can no longer be sold
options.d: Customers always pay after suppliers

questions.text: What is an accrued expense?

options.a: A cost incurred in a period but not yet paid in cash
options.b: An asset arising solely from future management intentions
options.c: Cash paid before the related service is delivered to the firm
options.d: A cash dividend paid from retained earnings

questions.text: Which is an example of a routine contractual accrued liability?

options.a: Inventory already sold for cash
options.b: Share premium received from investors
options.c: A patent acquired for cash
options.d: Wages earned by employees but not yet paid

questions.text: Why recognize accrued liabilities at the reporting date?

options.a: To postpone all expenses until cash is paid
options.b: To eliminate the balance-sheet accounting equation
options.c: To match incurred obligations and expenses to the correct reporting period
options.d: To turn unpaid interest into revenue

questions.text: What is deferred or unearned revenue?

options.a: Cash collected from a customer before the firm fulfills the related obligation
options.b: A non-cash asset impairment loss
options.c: Revenue recognized after delivery but not yet collected
options.d: An increase in shareholders' retained earnings

questions.text: What happens to deferred revenue when the company fulfills its promised service?

options.a: The amount is treated as financing income
options.b: The liability decreases and revenue is recognized
options.c: The liability doubles automatically
options.d: The company's inventory is always increased

questions.text: What distinguishes a warranty provision from a fixed invoice payable?

options.a: Its ultimate settlement depends on uncertain future product claims
options.b: It can only arise after a company is liquidated
options.c: It always requires no estimation
options.d: It is an equity contribution

questions.text: According to the lecture's provision-recognition rule, when should a contingent obligation be recognized?

options.a: Whenever a theoretical future dispute can be imagined
options.b: Only when the firm's share price falls
options.c: Only when cash is eventually paid
options.d: When a present obligation is probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated

questions.text: Why is a product warranty expense often recognized in the period of the sale?

options.a: Warranties are dividends to owners
options.b: The repair has already been paid in cash in every case
options.c: The sale creates the expected obligation to repair or replace defective goods
options.d: Warranty expenses are never recognized until settlement

questions.text: How does paying for a valid warranty repair affect an existing warranty provision?

options.a: It turns the liability into a trade receivable
options.b: It creates new contributed capital
options.c: It must increase current-period revenue
options.d: It reduces the previously recognized liability

questions.text: What is net working capital?

options.a: Sales minus cost of goods sold
options.b: Current assets minus current liabilities
options.c: Total assets minus shareholders' equity
options.d: Net profit minus dividends

questions.text: What does the current ratio measure?

options.a: Cash from financing divided by total debt
options.b: Current assets divided by current liabilities
options.c: Revenue divided by inventory
options.d: Current liabilities divided by non-current assets

questions.text: What might a current ratio below 1 indicate?

options.a: Current liabilities exceed current assets at the reporting date
options.b: All inventory is obsolete
options.c: Gross profit must be negative
options.d: The firm must be insolvent under every circumstance

questions.text: Why do firms in different industries require different levels of working capital?

options.a: Working capital is determined solely by the share price
options.b: Their operating cycles, payment terms, and inventory needs differ
options.c: Working capital is independent of operations
options.d: All firms must hold exactly the same inventory

questions.text: What does a revolving credit facility provide?

options.a: A fixed-price sale of inventory
options.b: A guarantee that interest rates never change
options.c: Access to borrowing up to a limit with a fluctuating outstanding balance
options.d: An immediate issuance of new ordinary shares

questions.text: What is the role of a letter of credit in commerce?

options.a: It represents the customer's net receivable balance
options.b: It eliminates the underlying purchase contract
options.c: A bank provides assurance of payment between buyer and supplier
options.d: It converts all supplier invoices into dividends

questions.text: What is a term loan?

options.a: Borrowing of an agreed principal amount with specified repayment terms
options.b: A guaranteed equity issue
options.c: A cash-equivalent security with no repayment requirement
options.d: A tax credit earned on future revenue

questions.text: Which feature commonly distinguishes a mortgage loan?

options.a: It is secured by collateral, often real estate
options.b: It gives the lender ordinary voting shares automatically
options.c: It is classified as retained earnings
options.d: It never requires interest

questions.text: What is a common reason firms issue corporate bonds?

options.a: To avoid all contractual interest and principal obligations
options.b: To raise substantial long-term funds from capital-market investors
options.c: To eliminate debt financing from the balance sheet
options.d: To reclassify inventory as goodwill

questions.text: What are the standard bondholder cash flows for an ordinary fixed-coupon bullet bond?

options.a: An infinite series of equal principal repayments without interest
options.b: Periodic coupon payments plus repayment of face value at maturity
options.c: Only a cash payment when the borrower makes a profit
options.d: Only an uncertain dividend at maturity

questions.text: How is the price of an ordinary fixed-coupon bond conceptually determined?

options.a: Present value of coupon payments plus present value of principal repayment
options.b: The issuer's current assets divided by current liabilities
options.c: Face value multiplied by the issuer's sales
options.d: Only the interest rate shown on the bond certificate

questions.text: What usually happens to the market price of a fixed-rate bond if comparable market yields rise?

options.a: It becomes identical to the issuer's share price
options.b: It remains exactly at par
options.c: It falls
options.d: It rises in the same proportion

questions.text: Why can a bond's market value change when its contractual coupon payments stay fixed?

options.a: The bond's original face value changes every day
options.b: Investors discount its promised cash flows using changing required yields
options.c: The company's sales always determine its coupon
options.d: The bond automatically converts into common equity

questions.text: What does the times-interest-earned ratio compare?

options.a: Accounts payable with inventory
options.b: Cash with current assets
options.c: Dividends with earnings per share
options.d: EBIT with gross interest expense

questions.text: What does a higher times-interest-earned ratio generally suggest?

options.a: Lower earnings before interest and tax by definition
options.b: Greater probability of failing every interest payment
options.c: Greater earnings coverage of contractual interest costs
options.d: Fewer total assets in every case

questions.text: What important limitation of times-interest-earned is highlighted in the lecture?

options.a: It measures earnings per ordinary share
options.b: It accounts for all future refinancing needs perfectly
options.c: It includes all cash and non-cash investing activities
options.d: It does not directly demonstrate the ability to repay debt principal

questions.text: What does cash from operations divided by total debt assess?

options.a: Cash generation relative to outstanding short- and long-term debt
options.b: Revenue growth per employee
options.c: The dividend yield on common shares
options.d: Capital expenditure as a fraction of sales

questions.text: Why might analysts subtract capital expenditure from operating cash before comparing it with debt?

options.a: Capital expenditure is always a financing inflow
options.b: Debt obligations can be paid exclusively with accounting profit
options.c: Capital expenditure never uses cash
options.d: Not all cash from operations remains available after maintaining or growing the asset base

questions.text: What is contributed share capital?

options.a: The sum of prior-period profits
options.b: Capital invested by owners in exchange for shares
options.c: An allowance for doubtful trade receivables
options.d: The amount of cash owed to lenders

questions.text: What does additional paid-in capital (share premium) generally represent?

options.a: The gain from selling inventories
options.b: Interest accrued on bonds
options.c: Share issue proceeds above nominal or par value
options.d: Accumulated unrealized foreign-exchange losses

questions.text: What is a common economic advantage of preferred shares over ordinary shares?

options.a: Mandatory voting control over all board seats
options.b: Priority to certain dividends or liquidation proceeds
options.c: A universal guarantee against any loss
options.d: The right to repayment ahead of all secured creditors

questions.text: What is a potential conversion feature of preferred shares?

options.a: The right to cancel all company liabilities
options.b: Automatic conversion of every company bond into inventories
options.c: The right to exchange preferred shares for a specified number of ordinary shares
options.d: A promise that preferred shares will not dilute ownership

questions.text: When does a non-controlling interest arise?

options.a: When all shareholders own identical amounts
options.b: When a parent consolidates a subsidiary it controls but does not own completely
options.c: When a firm holds cash in multiple currencies
options.d: Whenever a firm has any outstanding bond

questions.text: Why is non-controlling interest presented in consolidated equity?

options.a: It is always a future cash expense
options.b: Part of consolidated net assets belongs to owners other than the parent shareholders
options.c: It represents the parent company's trade payables
options.d: It is an intangible asset owned by suppliers

questions.text: What is retained earnings?

options.a: The fair value of every unrecognized brand
options.b: Cash issued for new share capital
options.c: Cumulative earned profit not distributed as dividends
options.d: Current-period revenue alone

questions.text: How do cash dividends affect retained earnings, all else equal?

options.a: They decrease retained earnings when recognized as distributions
options.b: They increase net income
options.c: They are classified as operating revenues
options.d: They increase the carrying amount of goodwill

questions.text: What does the statement of changes in equity help explain?

options.a: Only the repayment calendar of corporate bonds
options.b: Movements in equity from profit, OCI, distributions, and owner contributions
options.c: Only the net cash paid for inventory
options.d: Only sales growth of operating segments

questions.text: What is the dividend payout ratio usually expressed as?

options.a: Dividends relative to earnings
options.b: Share price divided by book value
options.c: Cost of goods sold relative to sales
options.d: Operating cash flow divided by capex

questions.text: What is dividend yield?

options.a: Total debt relative to the market value of debt
options.b: Market share relative to total sales
options.c: Net income relative to total assets
options.d: Dividends per share relative to current share price

questions.text: Why can a high dividend payout ratio warrant scrutiny?

options.a: It always eliminates the need for financing
options.b: It proves that future earnings will increase
options.c: It shows that all earnings are paid in cash at the same instant
options.d: It may leave fewer retained resources to support future investment

questions.text: What is book value per common share?

options.a: Cash flow from operations divided by debt
options.b: Common shareholders' book equity divided by common shares outstanding
options.c: Net income divided by total assets
options.d: Market capitalization divided by revenues

questions.text: Why may book value of equity differ substantially from market value?

options.a: Book value includes every internally generated intangible at market value
options.b: Both necessarily measure exactly the same thing
options.c: Market value excludes expectations about future profits
options.d: Accounting measures recognized net assets, whereas markets price expected future benefits and risks

questions.text: What happens to the accounting equation when a firm borrows cash from a bank?

options.a: Assets rise and equity falls by exactly the loan amount
options.b: Liabilities fall and assets rise by the loan amount
options.c: Assets and liabilities rise by equal amounts at initial recognition
options.d: Only net income increases

questions.text: What happens when a firm pays an existing supplier liability with cash?

options.a: Cash and accounts payable both decrease
options.b: Accounts payable becomes equity
options.c: Total assets increase and liabilities increase
options.d: Revenue and cash both increase

questions.text: Why are maturity profiles of borrowings relevant to credit analysis?

options.a: They reveal when refinancing or repayment pressure may arise
options.b: They precisely predict future market interest rates
options.c: They replace the need to analyze liquidity
options.d: They make all longer-term obligations current

questions.text: Why may a lower DPO sometimes signal financial strength rather than weakness?

options.a: The firm may be paying suppliers early to earn discounts or support relationships
options.b: DPO cannot reflect purchasing strategy
options.c: A lower DPO always proves supplier distress
options.d: DPO measures only interest-bearing debt

questions.text: How does extending supplier payment terms affect CCC mathematically, other inputs unchanged?

options.a: CCC must equal zero
options.b: CCC decreases because DPO is subtracted
options.c: CCC becomes identical to DSO
options.d: CCC increases because DPO is added

questions.text: What analytical mistake arises from treating all current liabilities as interest-bearing debt?

options.a: Shareholders' equity becomes negative by definition
options.b: The balance sheet no longer balances
options.c: Trade payables and operating accruals can be confused with borrowings
options.d: Cash receipts must equal revenue

questions.text: A buyer receives goods in December but will pay the supplier in January. Which reporting treatment is most consistent with accrual accounting?

options.a: Recognize customer revenue because cash has not been paid
options.b: Recognize a dividend in December
options.c: Delay all recognition until January cash payment
options.d: Recognize the relevant purchase/inventory and a payable in December

questions.text: A software provider collects a one-year subscription fee before providing the service. What is the appropriate initial treatment?

options.a: Recognize the entire amount as profit regardless of performance
options.b: Record an intangible impairment at contract inception
options.c: Recognize a contract liability and release it as service obligations are fulfilled
options.d: Treat the receipt as new common share capital

questions.text: A company has DSO of 45, DIO of 65, and DPO of 80 days. What is its cash conversion cycle?

options.a: 30 days
options.b: 190 days
options.c: -30 days
options.d: 110 days

questions.text: A bond was issued at a fixed coupon rate and new bonds of comparable risk now offer higher yields. Which market-value effect is most plausible?

options.a: The issuer's contractual principal disappears
options.b: The outstanding bond trades at a discount relative to its previous price
options.c: The bond automatically converts to preferred shares
options.d: The bond's contractual coupon increases automatically

questions.text: A firm earns an EBIT of €40 million and incurs gross interest expense of €20 million. Which interpretation best follows from times interest earned?

options.a: Its cash ratio is 2 times and all principal obligations are covered
options.b: Its current ratio is 0.5 regardless of balance-sheet totals
options.c: Its accrual-based interest coverage is 2 times, but principal repayment ability remains a separate concern
options.d: It earns €20 million of OCI by definition

questions.text: A parent company controls 70% of a subsidiary. How should the remaining 30% owned by outside shareholders be viewed in consolidated reporting?

options.a: As a decrease in all consolidated liabilities
options.b: As non-controlling interest in consolidated equity
options.c: As goodwill of exactly 30% of sales
options.d: As an increase in the parent's accounts receivable

questions.text: A firm pays a cash dividend using available bank deposits. Which pair of effects is most directly expected?

options.a: Higher operating earnings and lower bonds payable
options.b: Higher cash and higher total equity
options.c: Lower cash and lower total equity once the dividend is recognized and paid
options.d: Higher sales and lower current liabilities
